$Comment: A station is an ordered list of self-contained ACTIONS; this one has a single action, Mill, and everything about how milling runs is inside it. Nothing is inherited from anywhere else in the file - each group below carries its own $Comment explaining exactly what it does. Icon intentionally omitted: the engine falls back to the anchor block's own BlockType id at engage time when Identity.Icon is absent, and this jar's default Sawmill block shares the same id (RPG_Station_Sawmill, filename = item id), so the summary-HUD crest shows the block's own icon with zero duplicated id to drift. Every number in this file is a tunable leaf, and an ExtensionAsset carries real Puppet/Custody/ContributionScale keys with per-leaf overlay semantics, so a pack re-skinning this action authors only the leaves it re-tunes and inherits the rest of these defaults.

Block.$Comment: Exclusive true means one worker at a time - a property of the placed block, never of the job.

Actions.$Comment: Id 'Mill' is technically optional (an id-less entry answers to its array position), but authoring it is load-bearing: the id is what an ExtensionAsset targets (the sibling pack's contribution extension aims at exactly {Station 'Sawmill', Action 'Mill'}), what a custody claim records across a relog, and what stays stable when actions are reordered - a positional id changes the moment an action is inserted above it, which is the exact implicit-order fragility this schema exists to avoid. Author an Id on every action you expect anyone to extend.

Tool.$Comment: The ONE gate for this action: a Hatchet family match plus the Woods gather route, checked at engage and re-checked every heartbeat. The per-cycle durability drain rides in the same group because wear is a tool concern.

Recipe.$Comment: Authors only FromCrafting, never Conversions. The three Categories are genuine native recipe categories (every Wood_<Species>_{Planks,Decorative,Ornate}.json shares the same Wood_<Species>_Trunk ResourceTypeId input and the same Builders/StructuralCrafting bench, only the Category differs), so this is native-recipe composition, not invented content: the deriver surfaces 3 output categories per log species, 33 conversions in all, each stamped with its source category so sneak+F offers Planks/Decorative/Ornate for whatever log is loaded. A plain F press defaults to the FIRST authored Categories entry, so the array order (WoodPlanks first) is the default priority; reorder it to change that default, sneak+F still offers all three. Yield is purely DETERMINISTIC: Base 1 matches the native yield (every derived recipe in all three categories authors OutputQuantity 1 against a single-trunk input, true across all 11 wood species), so reading it tells you exactly what one cycle makes - everything conditional lives in Bonus below. A station deriving categories whose native recipes are NOT 1:1 should author Yield.Scale rather than Base, since the native quantity is not readable at the derivation seam.

Work.$Comment: CycleMs 4805 is the in-game-tuned milling cadence; MaxDurationMs caps a session at ten minutes; MaxMoveMeters is the walk-off distance that ends it.

Custody.$Comment: Placed-input custody: hold logs and press F to load up to 100 into the bench, then work from the pile instead of your backpack. States maps the claim lifecycle onto the block's own interaction states; Display renders the placed logs as a prop at the block top, Offset.Y -0.1 embedding them slightly into the bench (in-game-tuned).

Bonus.$Comment: Everything conditional or probabilistic about output lives here, as visible Rolls. Grants.OutputItems adds EXTRA units of the cycle's own product (the actual species being milled) - additive on top of Recipe.Yield, so the two numbers stay directly comparable and no file can silently multiply another's. The amount is FRACTIONAL: the whole part is granted every cycle and the fraction left over is the chance of one more, so 1.5 pays one plank always plus a second half the time. Everything the cycle grants is summed before that single resolution, so two rolls paying 0.5 each average one whole plank. Lootables pulls in three tables, each its own independently replaceable concern: SawmillFinds is the session-loyalty ladder any worker can reach, SawmillTrophy is the Sawmiller's Hatchet chase, and SawmillMasterworkFinds is the fourth find tier that chase pays out. Finds arrive as drop-list items and the trophy as a command grant, both different things from the planks these rolls add. A same-id Lootable in a later layer replaces a whole FILE, so which rolls share a file decides what a layering mod must inherit to re-tune one of them: these three are split so each can be replaced alone.

Rolls.$Comment: The tool ladder that pays for the milling time: a starter hatchet earns nothing extra and every upgrade is felt. Factors sum THREE tool axes because no two can rank the vanilla hatchet ladder alone: quality (the native ItemQuality.QualityValue - Junk 0, Common 1, Uncommon 2, Rare 3, Epic 4, Legendary 5) at weight 10.0 dominates, item level at 0.1 breaks ties inside a quality tier, and gather power at 1.0 rewards the genuinely better cutter. Quality alone cannot separate Wood/Crude from Copper (all three are Common); power alone cannot either (Wood and Copper share an identical 0.2 Woods power, and power SATURATES at 0.5 from the mid ladder up); item level separates them but must stay a small term because it does not track rarity (Onyxium is Epic at item level 4, so a level-led formula would rank it below a copper hatchet). The curve over the vanilla hatchets, counted on top of Recipe.Yield's one plank: Wood 10.6 and Crude 10.55 reach no floor (1 plank per cycle); Copper 11.3 reaches the 11 floor (2); Iron 22.3 reaches the 22 floor, whose FRACTIONAL 1.5 pays one plank always plus a second half the time, so Iron averages 2.5 rather than rounding onto a neighbouring tier and collapsing a rung; Thorium 33.5, Cobalt 34.0 and Adamantite 34.5 reach the 33 floor (3); Onyxium 40.9 and Mithril 45.5 reach the 40 floor (4); and the 50 floor (5 planks) is beyond every forgeable tool - only the sawmill's own drop-only Sawmiller's Hatchet (Legendary, scoring 55.55) or a better modded tool reaches it, making the trophy the bench's one endgame upgrade. A fractional floor value is the general route for any half-step tier, a modded one included: author it on the floor that earns it and it composes with every rung above and below, which a roll banded to one quality tier beside the ladder cannot do (a modded tool matching that tier while reaching a higher floor would collect both). Floors are NOT cumulative - the highest reached Min wins, and two floors sharing a Min is a validator warning since only the last authored one could ever be reached. Reweight Factors to change what the curve rewards, move a floor Min to change which tier earns which step, or append a floor for a modded tier above Epic.

The occasional windfall for everyone: chance = BasePercent 2 plus the held tool's gather power (a vanilla hatchet's Woods power is 0.2 to 0.5, so the real odds run 2.2 to 2.5 percent per cycle). CapPercent 25 is a safety ceiling that no vanilla tool approaches - it exists so a modded tool with an extreme power value cannot turn the windfall into a guarantee.

ContributionScale.$Comment: Not loot: this ladder scales the action's per-cycle CONTRIBUTIONS - the namespaced amounts a listening mod attaches to this action (this jar attaches none itself; its content is progression-free by design, so the scale sits ready for whichever mod adds them). Same three factors and the same 11/22/33/40 crossings as the plank ladder above, so a tool that doubles your planks also doubles the attached amounts: below 11 the amount forwards unscaled, Copper-tier x2.0, Iron-tier x2.5, Cobalt-tier x3.0, Mithril-tier x4.0, and x5.0 at the 50 floor only the drop-only Sawmiller's Hatchet reaches - the contribution curve tracks the plank curve at every rung including the trophy's. The ENGINE pre-scales before the cycle event dispatches and reports the multiplier for display only, so a listener grants the forwarded amount verbatim and can neither forget the curve nor apply it twice.

Worker.$Comment: How the person looks doing this - all in-game-tuned standalone defaults. Hold seats the worker on the block mount and interrupts on damage; Animation drives the swing cadence (the work clip is the held hatchet's own default Action-slot clip, re-fired every IntervalMs so a viewer arriving mid-session sees it within one interval); Puppet spawns the visible working double (Offset.Z 1.0 and Yaw 0.0 place it at the bench, the real player hidden by scale, the held item mirrored into its hand).

Moments.$Comment: What it sounds and looks like at the two fixed times: Cycle plays once per completed conversion, Completion once when the session ends. Both are Presentation groups a flair can re-skin per moment id.
